claims.text: Sarvottam Cables reported Q1 revenue from operations of ₹1,428 crore, a 35% increase from the year-ago period
Sarvottam Cables Q1 net profit rose about 6% to ₹82 crore
Sarvottam Cables operating margins contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2%
Copper prices rose nearly 14% during the quarter
A Mumbai-based analyst stated that the volume story is intact, but investors will watch whether the company can pass on higher copper costs
Sarvottam Cables shares fell 3.2% to ₹1,012 on the NSE on Friday following the results
Sarvottam Cables is maintaining its FY27 full-year revenue growth guidance of 15 to 17 percent
The Bharuch facility will contribute to revenue from the second half of FY27
Data-centre cables account for about 9 percent of domestic revenue
Management expects data-centre cable revenue share can double in two years
Margin contraction was mostly due to copper costs
About two-thirds of contracts have price-variation clauses that reset with a lag of one to two quarters
The company is not seeing irrational pricing from competitors
Receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year
The increase in receivable days is mainly due to two large state utility customers where payments are slower
The company has not seen any customer defaults
Total capex for the Bharuch plant is ₹620 crore, of which about 70 percent is already spent
Bharuch capex is funded mainly through internal accruals and some term debt
Net debt to equity is 0.35 times
Revenue from operations was ₹1,248 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹1,058 crore in Q1 FY26, up 18.0%
EBITDA was ₹140 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹136 crore in Q1 FY26, up 2.6%
EBITDA margin was 11.2% in Q1 FY27 compared to 12.9% in Q1 FY26, down 170 bps
Profit after tax was ₹82 crore in Q1 FY27 compared to ₹77 crore in Q1 FY26, up 5.9%
Order book stood at ₹3,900 crore as of 30 June 2026, up from ₹3,150 crore a year ago
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27 compared to 16% in Q1 FY26
The new Bharuch plant will add about 30% to cable capacity
The Bharuch plant is on track to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27
MD Anil Deshpande stated demand from power transmission and data-centre projects remains strong
Management expects to pass on copper price increases to customers over the next two quarters
Promoter pledged holding at Sarvottam Cables rose to 35% as of March 2024, up from 22% six months prior
Market Watch India reported high promoter pledging is often seen as a risk for minority shareholders
Sarvottam Cables received an order from the Joint Commissioner, CGST, Mumbai raising a demand of ₹46.3 crore including interest and penalty
The GST demand relates to input tax credit claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22
The company believes it has a strong case on merits based on legal advice and intends to file an appeal
The company does not expect any material impact on its financial position or operations from the GST demand
Promoters & promoter group held 58.2% of shares as of June 2026, 58.2% as of March 2026, and 58.4% as of June 2025
Pledged shares as a percentage of promoter holding were 4.1% in June 2026, 6.0% in March 2026, and 11.5% in June 2025
FII holding was 11.8% in June 2026, 10.9% in March 2026, and 9.2% in June 2025
DII holding was 14.6% in June 2026, 14.1% in March 2026, and 12.7% in June 2025
Public and others holding was 15.4% in June 2026, 16.8% in March 2026, and 19.7% in June 2025
